title: Fly to Ratti Gali, the jewel of Neelum
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: In the far north of Azad Kashmir lies the Neelum Valley, one of the greenest corners of Pakistan.
Let's fly up from the Neelum River, towards one of its most famous lakes.
The route starts near the village of Dowarian. From there, a jeep track and then a hike lead up into the mountains.
Ahead lies Ratti Gali Lake, about three thousand seven hundred metres above sea level.
It is an alpine lake, fed by melting snow and glaciers on the peaks around it.
In summer, the meadows around the lake fill with wildflowers, such as primulas and gentians.
The area is home to the colourful Himalayan monal pheasant, and even the Himalayan brown bear.
For most of the year, the lake is frozen and cut off by snow. It is usually reached only from about July to September.
Visitors often camp at the base camp below, and walk up to the lake in the early morning.
In July twenty twenty-four, two tourists were killed when a jeep heading for Ratti Gali fell into a water channel, and officials began a crackdown on unfit vehicles.
As tourism grows, visitors are being urged to keep the lake clean, and take their rubbish home.
